title: Council and committee appointments for the 2022–2026 term
subtitle: Public advisory appointments, larger library board, Heritage Guelph councillor seat, and Elliott management committee changes.
overview: Council made its public appointments to advisory committees, local boards and commissions for the new term, following a closed session on the candidates. Council also asked staff to keep recruiting for remaining vacancies and dissolved the Guelph Sports Hall of Fame Board of Directors at the board's own request {{vote:m2}}.

Councillors then chose chairs and vice-chairs for the Committee of the Whole service areas and named council members to outside boards, including the Grand River Conservation Authority, the Police Services Board, the Public Health board and the Downtown Guelph Business Association.

Council also changed some structures. The Guelph Public Library Board will now include three council members and 10 public members {{vote:m18}}. A councillor will sit on Heritage Guelph as a non-voting member {{vote:m24}}. The Committee of Management for The Elliott was expanded to include the service area vice-chairs and others {{vote:m14}}. These changes affect how council and its boards communicate on budgets and local decisions.

decisions.detail: Council appointed and reappointed residents to advisory committees, boards and commissions, directed further recruitment for vacancies, and dissolved the Guelph Sports Hall of Fame Board at its request.
Council reappointed four members and appointed five new members to Heritage Guelph.
The Guelph Public Library Board was changed to 10 public members and 3 council members.
Councillor Downer was appointed to Heritage Guelph as a non-voting member for a term ending November 2024.
Council waived the appointment policy and Heritage Guelph terms of reference so a non-voting councillor could be appointed.

decisions.item: Committee of Management for The Elliott
decisions.detail: The committee's composition was amended to include the service area vice-chairs, the Public Services chair and the council appointee to The Elliott's board.
Councillor Caron was named chair of Corporate Services, with other service area chairs and vice-chairs appointed in separate motions.
Mayor Guthrie and Councillor Allt were appointed to the Guelph Police Services Board for a term ending November 15, 2026.

debate: Before the closed session, one councillor declared a conflict of interest because a family member had applied, and was kept out of that discussion and the related votes.

For the Corporate Services vice-chair, two councillors made short pitches. One cited project management and technology experience and interest in the city's website redesign. The other cited public-sector, human resources, audit and budget experience.

A councillor asked whether a person serving as vice-chair of two committees would leave the Committee of Management for The Elliott short a member. Staff said council could amend that motion to add another member if needed.

The mover of the library board change said more council members would improve communication with council and give council more input into the budget, especially as the new main library branch is built. The Police Services Board and Public Health already have more than one council member.

On Heritage Guelph, a councillor said a past facilitation report recommended a council member sit on the committee to improve collaboration. The councillor said changes expected from provincial Bill 23 made this a good time.
